chapter: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
title: Quitting for the Savoy in New York at lower pay
summary: Wanting to reach New York, he left Buffalo to join the Savoy band with R. Q. Dixon and Jimmy Smith, doubling at the Harlem Opera House, but then earned only $22.50 and went back to Buffalo.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But this guy sends for me -- I always wanted to come to New York -- so this guy sends for me, I'll go down here, you know.
So you quit to go down.

Yeah, I quit to go down to work with him, you know, and I come down to find out the money wasn't as much as I was getting in Buffalo, and we also played at the Harlem Opera House, that first week at the Harlem Opera House, and the --
Savoy?
Savoy, we doubled. So that was great. That was pretty good bread.
That was good money, yeah.
For two jobs, but then the next week I didn't get but $22.50, so I didn't like that.
Well, who was in that band?

I can't think of all the guys. One of them was R. Q. Dixon, because he was sitting right next to me; a trumpet player. And another one was a guy named Ted Colon. He was in it. And naturally Jimmy Smith on the bass.
Were you playing opposite Chick?
I think it was Chick, yeah.
Yeah.
I think it was Chick's band.
Yeah.
Because that's when I first seen that little trumpet player named Hunt. Remember a trumpet player with Chick named Hunt? [Louis Hunt]
No.
I can't think of his first name.
No, no, I don't remember him.

And we did that, and then after that two weeks was up, I said I've got to go back to Buffalo and straighten my business out around there, and they said, 'Well, you don't have to take your horn.' I said, 'No, no, I take my
horn everywhere I go." I never come back. I went on back with Stuff.
